**Addressing @ardaguclu review feedback:**

**1 & 2. Removed `keepAliveInterval` field, using constant directly** ✅

Done in [874d0159a](https://github.com/openshift/oc/pull/2288/commits/874d0159a). The `keepAliveInterval` field has been removed from `MustGatherOptions` and `defaultKeepAliveInterval` is now used directly in the ticker:

```go
ticker := time.NewTicker(defaultKeepAliveInterval)
```

**3. Confirmed: `klog.V(2)` works correctly from inside a goroutine** ✅

Tested by pointing the keep-alive goroutine at a fake API server returning 401 Unauthorized:

```
I0722 16:26:44.469439  48298 klog_goroutine_check.go:43] keep-alive probe failed (non-fatal): the server has asked for the client to provide credentials
I0722 16:26:45.466094  48298 klog_goroutine_check.go:43] keep-alive probe failed (non-fatal): the server has asked for the client to provide credentials
I0722 16:26:46.467053  48298 klog_goroutine_check.go:43] keep-alive probe failed (non-fatal): the server has asked for the client to provide credentials
```

`klog` is goroutine-safe by design — it uses internal `sync.Mutex` for all write operations. It is used from goroutines extensively throughout the Kubernetes codebase (informers, controllers, watchers, etc.).

Thanks @ardaguclu — removed the `TestStartClientKeepAlive` tests in 026afc1bb.

As you noted, these tests were essentially testing Go's `time.Ticker` + `context.Done()` semantics rather than meaningful business logic. The keep-alive behaviour is simple, deterministic, and fully covered by the existing end-to-end evidence (token stays alive across a 6-minute idle window with `accessTokenInactivityTimeout: 300s`).

All four review items are now addressed:
1. ✅ Removed the `keepAliveInterval` field — using the constant directly
2. ✅ Using `defaultKeepAliveInterval` directly in the ticker
3. ✅ Confirmed `klog.V(2).Infof` is safe from goroutines (klog is goroutine-safe by design)
4. ✅ Removed the unit tests — timer semantics don't need testing here

Great catch @ardaguclu — you're absolutely right. Fixed in 4b21c7d59.

**Before:** `startClientKeepAlive` was called inside `processNextWorkItem`, which runs once per gather pod. With N images, we'd spawn N identical goroutines all pinging the same API server.

**After:** A single `startClientKeepAlive` call in `Run()`, started before the worker goroutines and stopped after `wg.Wait()` returns. One goroutine covers the entire session since we always talk to the same cluster.

```go
// In Run() — single instance for the whole session
keepAliveCtx, stopKeepAlive := context.WithCancel(ctx)
defer stopKeepAlive()
o.startClientKeepAlive(keepAliveCtx)

wg.Add(concurrentMG)
// ... worker goroutines ...
wg.Wait()
stopKeepAlive()
```

### Test 2: End-to-end — must-gather survives past the 5-minute token inactivity timeout

**Setup:**
```bash
# Cluster: OCP 4.22.3 (fresh install, ~1 hour old)
oc patch oauth cluster --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"tokenConfig":{"accessTokenInactivityTimeout":"300s"}}}'
```

In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/oc/pull/2288):

>## Summary
>
>Add a client-side keep-alive mechanism to `oc adm must-gather` that prevents OAuth access token
>revocation due to `accessTokenInactivityTimeout` on hardened clusters.
>
>**Problem:** When `accessTokenInactivityTimeout` is configured (e.g., 300s for regulated
>environments), `oc adm must-gather` fails with "Unauthorized" errors mid-collection. The root
>cause is that the `oc` client holds a single long-lived HTTP log-follow stream to watch the
>gather pod. The API server does not count this persistent connection as "activity" for the OAuth
>inactivity timer, causing the token to be revoked.
>
>**Fix:** A background goroutine that calls `Discovery().ServerVersion()` (authenticated
>GET /version) every 30 seconds during the gather lifecycle. This resets the OAuth inactivity
>timer on each call, keeping the session alive for the full duration of the operation.
>
>Resolves: [RFE-8595](https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/RFE-8595)
>
>## What Changed
>
>Two additions to `pkg/cli/admin/mustgather/mustgather.go`:
>
>1. **`startClientKeepAlive(ctx)`** — Background goroutine making periodic authenticated API
>   probes (every 30s) to reset the OAuth token inactivity timer.
>
>2. **Integration in `processNextWorkItem()`** — Started after pod creation, stopped via
>   `defer` after data copy completes. Covers: pod startup wait -> log streaming -> gather
>   completion wait -> rsync download.
>
>```go
>stopKeepAlive := o.startClientKeepAlive(ctx)
>defer stopKeepAlive()
>```
>
>## Test Evidence
>
>### Environment
>- **Cluster:** OCP 4.20.0 (Kubernetes v1.33.11)
>- **OAuth config:** `accessTokenInactivityTimeout: 300s`
>- **Token:** `inactivityTimeoutSeconds: 300` (confirmed on OAuthAccessToken object)
>- **Test scenario:** `sleep 360` (6-min idle gap) injected before `/usr/bin/gather`
>  — forces a window with zero client-side API calls, exceeding the 5-minute timeout
>
>### WITHOUT the fix (unpatched oc)
>
>```
>$ ./oc-unpatched adm must-gather --timeout=15m \
>    -- '/bin/bash -c "echo GATHER_START; sleep 360; echo GATHER_AFTER_SLEEP; /usr/bin/gather"'
>
>[must-gather-5npp9] POD 05:30:13Z GATHER_START
>[must-gather-5npp9] POD 05:36:13Z GATHER_AFTER_SLEEP
>[must-gather-5npp9] OUT 05:43:22Z gather logs unavailable: Unauthorized
>[must-gather-5npp9] OUT 05:43:22Z waiting for gather to complete
>[must-gather-5npp9] OUT 05:58:22Z gather never finished: context deadline exceeded
>Unauthorized
>error getting cluster version: Unauthorized
>error getting cluster operators: Unauthorized
>error: gather never finished for pod must-gather-5npp9: context deadline exceeded
>```
>
>| Metric | Result |
>|--------|--------|
>| Exit code | **1 (FAILURE)** |
>| Duration | 28 min (hung on deadline) |
>| Data collected | **12 KB (3 files - empty shell)** |
>| Unauthorized errors | **4** |
>
>### WITH the fix (patched oc - keep-alive enabled)
>
>```
>$ ./oc adm must-gather --timeout=15m \
>    -- '/bin/bash -c "echo GATHER_START; sleep 360; echo GATHER_AFTER_SLEEP; /usr/bin/gather"'
>
>[must-gather-7cv6s] POD 04:04:28Z GATHER_START
>[must-gather-7cv6s] POD 04:10:28Z GATHER_AFTER_SLEEP
>[must-gather-7cv6s] OUT 04:17:29Z waiting for gather to complete
>[must-gather-7cv6s] OUT 04:17:29Z downloading gather output
>... (full collection completes successfully) ...
>```
>
>| Metric | Result |
>|--------|--------|
>| Exit code | **0 (SUCCESS)** |
>| Duration | 37 min |
>| Data collected | **6.4 GB (8,489 files)** |
>| Unauthorized errors | **0** |
>
>### Comparative Summary
>
>| | Without Fix | With Fix |
>|---|---|---|
>| Exit code | 1 (failure) | 0 (success) |
>| Data collected | 12 KB | 6.4 GB |
>| Files | 3 | 8,489 |
>| Unauthorized errors | 4 | 0 |
>| Token survived 300s policy? | Revoked at ~5 min | Alive for 37 min |
>
>### Unit Tests
>
>```
>$ go test ./pkg/cli/admin/mustgather/ -v -count=1
>
>=== RUN   TestStartClientKeepAlive
>=== RUN   TestStartClientKeepAlive/makes_periodic_authenticated_API_calls
>=== RUN   TestStartClientKeepAlive/stops_when_cancel_is_called
>--- PASS: TestStartClientKeepAlive (35.10s)
>PASS
>ok      github.com/openshift/oc/pkg/cli/admin/mustgather    37.265s
>```
>
>## Use Case
>
>This addresses environments where short `accessTokenInactivityTimeout` values (e.g., 5-10
>minutes) are mandated by regulatory or security compliance policies (Banking, Government,
>PCI-DSS). Previously, administrators in such environments could not run `oc adm must-gather`
>without either:
>- Temporarily relaxing the timeout (violating security policy), or
>- Running a manual workaround (`while true; do oc whoami; sleep 60; done`) in the background
>
>This fix eliminates both workarounds by building the equivalent heartbeat directly into `oc`.
>
>## Design Decisions
>
>- **30s interval** — Well within any reasonable timeout (minimum ~60s), fires ~10 times before
>  a 5-minute timeout would expire
>- **`Discovery().ServerVersion()`** — Lightest possible authenticated API call; single GET,
>  no list/watch, no resource creation
>- **Non-fatal errors** — Probe failures are logged at V(5) only; transient network blips
>  won't kill the gather
>- **Lifecycle scoped** — Starts at pod creation, stops at data download completion via `defer`
>- **Zero configuration** — Always-on, no flags needed, fully backward-compatible
>- **No cluster-side changes** — Entirely client-side fix; no admin action required on the cluster
>
>## How to Reproduce
>
>```bash
># 1. Set 5-min inactivity timeout
>oc patch oauth.config.openshift.io cluster --type=merge \
>  -p '{"spec":{"tokenConfig":{"accessTokenInactivityTimeout":"300s"}}}'
>
># 2. Wait for rollout
>oc rollout status deployment/oauth-openshift -n openshift-authentication --timeout=300s
>
># 3. Force fresh login (new token gets the policy)
>oc logout && oc login -u <user> -p <pass> <api-url> --insecure-skip-tls-verify
>
># 4. Run must-gather with idle gap exceeding timeout
>oc adm must-gather --timeout=15m \
>  -- '/bin/bash -c "sleep 360; /usr/bin/gather"'
>
># 5. Restore
>oc patch oauth.config.openshift.io cluster --type=json \
>  -p '[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/tokenConfig"}]'
>```
>
